results.title: Summer Humanities and Arts Research Program (SHARP)
results.content: The intent of the program is to provide a formative and substantive research experience over ten weeks of the summer, working full-time (40 hours per week) on a project designed by specified Harvard faculty or in collaboration with partnering libraries and museums. For SHARP independent research projects, applicants must describe the proposed research project in detail and the scope of the work for the 10-week summer research period, including specific information about the resources and materials to be engaged on campus. By the end of the program, the fellow should have knowledge of Harvard Art Museums collections, improved research and writing skills, familiarity with different models for public engagement in museums, and experience creating and distributing educational materials for museums. **SHARP is a Harvard Summer Undergraduate Research Village Program (HSURV).** HSURV programs provide a research experience with Harvard-affiliated faculty mentors, along with a stipend and on-campus housing and a partial meal plan for 9 weeks over the summer.

results.title: Artificial Intelligence and Culture
results.content: The Report is structured into seven thematic sections, offering a global, multidisciplinary perspective: • Ethical landscape of AI in culture • Cultural rights in the digital age • AI and cultural value chains in the creative economy • AI and cultural education • Culture, climate and environmental sustainability • Heritage at risk and AI • AI, freedom and sovereignty This Report reflects both academic research and practical experience and is grounded in UNESCO’s evolving normative ecosystem. She is a member of the UNESCO Global Expert Panel on the 2005 Convention on Cultural Expressions and as part of this role, she has delivered global research and advisory support to state parties on emerging technologies (including AI) in the global creative industries. She is a member of UNESCO’s Global Reference Group on Diversity of Cultural Expressions in the Digital Environment - supporting the development of frameworks for supporting the sector in the age of technologies like AI.

results.title: Policy advice and best practices on bias and fairness in AI
results.content: The first objective of this paper is to concisely survey the state-of-the-art of fair-AI methods and resources, and the main policies on bias in AI, with the aim of providing such a bird’s-eye guidance for both researchers and practitioners. We take a bird’s-eye view of the methods and resources, with links to specialized surveys, and of the issues and challenges related to policies on bias and fairness in AI. Biases in AI algorithms have similar foundations as human cognitive biases, namely the reliance on heuristic algorithmic-search strategies that work well on average (Hellström et al., 2020. Several categorizations of the sources of bias and fairness in AI have been proposed in contexts such as social data (Olteanu et al., 2019. ACM Transactions on Information Systems, 41(3), 1–39.")), algorithmic hiring (Fabris et al., 2023. Fairness in AI (or simply, *fair-AI*) aims at designing methods for detecting, mitigating, and controlling biases in AI-supported decision making (Schwartz et al., 2022. *et al.* Policy advice and best practices on bias and fairness in AI.
